text: The officer told investigators that he had seen the echo forty minutes before the encounter.
The master confirmed that he had read it during his last certificate renewal.
He stated that the lookout had been stood down at midnight.
Rule 19 states that a vessel shall determine whether a close-quarters situation is developing.
Neither vessel altered course, and no sound signal was made at the prescribed intervals.
Rule 19 states that a vessel shall take avoiding action in ample time.
In restricted visibility there is no stand-on vessel, and both ships are required to act.
The report concludes that a proper lookout was not maintained.

I had the echo at two o'clock, maybe a little after. It was steady, fine on the starboard bow, and I plotted it twice. I judged that she was crossing and that under the rules she was the one who had to keep out of my way, so I held my course. I know now that that was wrong, and I have said so. In fog the crossing rules do not apply at all. Both of us should have slowed down and both of us should have been sounding. What I will not accept is the suggestion that there was nobody on lookout. I have told the investigators the same thing four times: the lookout was stood down at midnight because the master told me to send him to the forward store, and if that is denied, then one of us is not remembering the night the way it happened.

Candidates lose marks on Rule 19 for one reason: they read it as if it were the crossing rule with fog added. It is not. Rule 19 applies when vessels are not in sight of one another in or near an area of restricted visibility, and it replaces the steering rules entirely. There is no give-way vessel and there is no stand-on vessel. Every vessel shall proceed at a safe speed adapted to the prevailing circumstances. Every vessel which detects another by radar alone shall determine whether a close-quarters situation is developing, and if so shall take avoiding action in ample time. And note the word shall. In this document shall is not the future. It is an obligation, and there is no version of the rule in which it is optional. If you can say those three things, you can answer any question they set on Rule 19.
